result.question: Why do leprous men go to Arameans?

readings.support: So come now, let us go over to the camp of the Arameans. If they let us live, we will live

readings.answer: Because staying or going into the city meant certain death (from famine).
readings.support: If we say, ‘Let us go into the city,’ we will die there from the famine in the city; but if we sit here, we will also die

assessments.reason: The men say, “If they let us live, we will live; if they kill us, we will die,” which supports going for a chance to live; this is a valid but differently framed rationale than the key’s focus on death if they stay.

“If we… go into the city, we will die… if we sit here, we will also die” shows staying meant death; this matches the key’s reason (despite ‘might’ vs ‘will’) that the prospect of death if they stayed drove them to go.
